questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: While speaking to a friend, which of the following parameters holds a unique value in the sound produced?
questions.solution:
The frequency of a sound wave depends only on the source producing it and remains constant even if the medium changes. It is a fundamental characteristic of the speaker's vocal cords. Therefore, while speaking to a friend, the frequency of the sound produced holds a unique value.

Wave velocity depends on the properties of the medium.

Wavelength depends on both the frequency and the medium.

Amplitude depends on the energy or loudness of the sound, which can vary continuously.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A source of sound travels towards an observer.
options: The frequency of the source increases.
The vibration amplitude of the particles increases.
The speed of sound in the medium increases.
The wavelength of the sound in the medium towards the observer decreases.
questions.solution:
When a source of sound moves towards an observer, the successive wavefronts emitted by the source are compressed in the direction of motion.

The apparent wavelength $\lambda'$ in the medium towards the observer is given by $\lambda' = \dfrac{v - v_s}{f}$, where $v$ is the speed of sound in the medium, $v_s$ is the speed of the source, and $f$ is the actual frequency of the source.

Since $v_s > 0$, we have $\lambda' < \lambda$. Thus, the wavelength of the sound in the medium towards the observer decreases.

The actual frequency of the source and the speed of sound in the medium depend on the source characteristics and medium properties respectively, and remain unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A listener is stationary with respect to a source of sound. A wind begins blowing along the line connecting the source and the observer. Which of the following quantities remain unchanged?
questions.solution:
Let $v$ be the velocity of sound in still air, $v_w$ be the velocity of wind, and $f_0$ be the frequency of the source.

Since the source is stationary, the effective velocity of sound relative to the ground becomes $v' = v \pm v_w$.

The wavelength of the sound waves is given by $\lambda' = \dfrac{v'}{f_0} = \dfrac{v \pm v_w}{f_0}$. Thus, the wavelength changes.

The listener is also stationary, so the speed of sound relative to the listener is $v'$.

The frequency observed by the listener is $f' = \dfrac{v'}{\lambda'} = \dfrac{v \pm v_w}{\dfrac{v \pm v_w}{f_0}} = f_0$.

Thus, the frequency remains unchanged.

Since the time period is the reciprocal of frequency ($T = \dfrac{1}{f}$), the time period also remains unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vibrating organ pipe has a fundamental frequency equal to $200 \text{ Hz}$.
options: The first overtone is exactly $400 \text{ Hz}$.
The first overtone could be $400 \text{ Hz}$.
A frequency of $600 \text{ Hz}$ is an overtone.
The first overtone could be $600 \text{ Hz}$.
questions.solution:
The organ pipe can be open at both ends or closed at one end.

For an open organ pipe, the frequencies of harmonics are given by $f = n f_0$, where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$
The fundamental frequency is $f_0 = 200 \text{ Hz}$.
The frequencies are $200 \text{ Hz}, 400 \text{ Hz}, 600 \text{ Hz}, \dots$
The first overtone is $400 \text{ Hz}$ and the second overtone is $600 \text{ Hz}$.

For a closed organ pipe, the frequencies of harmonics are given by $f = (2n-1) f_0$, where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$
The frequencies are $200 \text{ Hz}, 600 \text{ Hz}, 1000 \text{ Hz}, \dots$
The first overtone is $600 \text{ Hz}$.

Thus, the first overtone could be $400 \text{ Hz}$ (if the pipe is open) or $600 \text{ Hz}$ (if the pipe is closed).
In both cases, $600 \text{ Hz}$ is an overtone (second overtone for open pipe, first overtone for closed pipe).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electrically maintained tuning fork oscillates with a constant frequency and a constant amplitude. When the temperature of the surrounding air rises while the pressure is kept constant, the produced sound will exhibit
questions.solution:
The frequency of the sound produced is determined by the source, which is the electrically maintained tuning fork. Since it oscillates with a constant frequency, the frequency $f$ and time period $T$ of the produced sound remain constant.

The velocity of sound in a gas is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma RT}{M}}$.

As the temperature $T$ of the surrounding air increases, the velocity of sound $v$ increases.

The wavelength of the sound wave is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f}$.

Since $v$ increases and $f$ is constant, the wavelength $\lambda$ also increases.

Therefore, the sound will exhibit a larger wavelength and a larger velocity.
